exec: Japan's police now have a dedicated team that can go to a cyberattack victim and preserve evidence; relevant to firms operating in Japan.
plain: Japan's National Police Agency started a team that goes to cyberattack victims, works with prefectural police and collects and preserves access logs, and advises on limiting damage and restoring systems.
summary: According to ビジネス+IT, Japan's National Police Agency established the Fast Forensic Force (FFF), an initial-response investigation and forensics unit for cyberattacks, on 20 November, with a launch ceremony that day. It is to go to the scene at the request of a victim or a prefectural police force, collect and preserve communication logs that give clues to the unauthorized access, and advise on limiting damage and restoring systems. The article gives 153 personnel in total.
title: Japan's National Police Agency launches Fast Forensic Force for cyberattack response

validation.note: Only ビジネス+IT read (partly members-only); NPA's own release not found by search.

review.note: Compared with sbbit article: 20 Nov launch, dispatch on victim or prefectural request, 153 total, advice all match. Summary said logs show how intruders got in; source says logs that are clues to unauthorized access. Reworded summary and plain.
